coord_notes.kind: The trained model is \(f(W'+X)\) with the original architecture: LoRA's additive rank-\(r\) update, but the iterate is the point \(X\in\mathcal M_r\) itself and the frozen weight is shifted to \(W'=W_0-X_0\) (LOI).
coord_notes.shape: \((W_0-X_0)+\mathcal M_{\le r}\): LoRA's cone translated to the vertex \(W_0-X_0\), with \(X_0=\alpha U_{1:r}V_{r+1:2r}^\top\) of rank \(r\), so \(\theta_0\) is a smooth point (stratum S, as LoRA-GA). The paper's zero-init variant is LoRA's apex cone instead.
coord_notes.base_point: \(S_1=T_{X_0}\mathcal M_r\), of dimension \(r(m+n-r)=d\): regular (Thm II.2(b), stratum S), and \(W'+X_0=W_0\) exactly.
coord_notes.gauge: The trained variable is the point \(X\in\mathcal M_r=(\mathbb R^{m\times r}_*\times\mathbb R^{r\times n}_*)/GL_r\), so \(\rho\) is an embedding. The thin-factor storage carries a \(GL_r\) fibre that no step sees (tangent projection, Muon direction and truncated-SVD retraction are computed on the quotient): the gauge is quotiented out, not merely respected (with the factors read as \(Q\) it would be \(GL_r\), all of it respected, as undamped scaled GD).
coord_notes.covariance: LOI uses bare singular frames of \(\nabla_W\mathcal L(W_0)\) without singular values: scale-invariant, \(O(m)\times O(n)\) as for LoRA-GA, coded OxO. The Muon polar factor is \(O\times O\)-equivariant as well; the zero-init variant would be GLxGL.
coord_notes.merge: \(W'+X_T\) is one dense matrix stored as thin factors, as for LoRA.
coord_notes.rebasing: A fixed-rank shape closed under scaling: \(\to\Theta\) after \(\lceil\min(m,n)/r\rceil\) merges, as LoRA (Thm V.3(a)).

methods.categorical_reading: Riemannion changes the object and not only the metric: its parameter space is the fixed-rank manifold \(\mathcal M_r\), the quotient of LoRA's factor space by \(GL_r\), so \(\rho\) is an embedding and the gauge question disappears instead of being answered by a gauge-respecting cometric (scaled GD, Thm III.12(c)). LOI is a Type II pointing: the rank-\(r\) start \(\alpha U_{1:r}V_{r+1:2r}^\top\) in the gradient's top-\(2r\) frame with a compensated residual, the mirrored member of the family that contains LoRA-GA's start.

arrows.note: LOI instance. Thm II.1 conversion: Riemannion_r into LoRA_{2r} on the untouched W_0, at the degenerate pointing ([B_0,-B_0],[A_0;A_0]) (product 0, as for LoRA-GA and PiSSA). The first block is a smooth local section of the quotient map near X_0 (rank r), with h(X_0) = ([B_0,-B_0],[A_0;A_0]); checked numerically (error 2e-15). With the stored thin factors (B,A) it reads h(B,A) = ([B,-B_0],[A;A_0]).

obstructions.reason: Different points of stratum S: LOI's vertex W_0 - alpha U_{1:r}V_{r+1:2r}^T against LoRA-GA's W_0 - P_GA with P_GA proportional to U_{r+1:2r}V_{1:r}^T (the paper's own Thm 5.1 contains both; it uses the mirrored member). Translated cones with distinct vertices are not nested (Thm II.2(a),(d)).
LOI instance: a smooth Type II start against LoRA's T_A apex at equal rank, so the images are incomparable (Thm II.2(d)). The paper's zero-init variant is LoRA itself (h = id).

Arrow checked numerically: rho_LoRA(h(X)) = W'+X for X on M_r near X_0 (2e-16), h(X_0) = ([B_0,-B_0],[A_0;A_0]) (1e-16), thin-factor form likewise; matches the LoRA-GA/PiSSA -> LoRA precedent. coord_notes.kind: A merge-and-restart scheme of two-sided action methods: each round trains \(W\mapsto P_k^\top W_{k-1}R_k^\top\) (convention \(y=Wx\): \(R_k\in O(d_{in})\) on the input side, \(P_k\in O(d_{out})\) on the output side), merges every 400 steps, resets \(Q=0\) and redraws the permutations. \(\theta_0\) is a random initialisation (pretraining), not a pretrained weight.
coord_notes.shape: Per round the orbit of \(W_{k-1}\) under permutation-conjugated block-diagonal factors on both sides. With exact Cayley it lies in \(O(m)W_{k-1}O(n)\) (spectrum fixed); the released Cayley–Neumann factor \((I+Q)(I+Q+Q^2+Q^3)=C(Q)(I-Q^4)\) is only quasi-orthogonal, \(R^\top R=(I-Q^4)^2\) (both checked to \(10^{-16}\)), coded Orb as OFTv2.
coord_notes.base_point: At \(Q=0\), \(\dim S_1=\tfrac{b-1}2(d_{in}+d_{out})\), the number of skew parameters, for generic \(W\) (checked: 30 of 30 at \(m=8,n=12,b=4\)): regular, every round starting at \(W_{k-1}\).
coord_notes.gauge: None: the per-round orbit map has full rank at \(Q=0\) and at generic \(Q\) (checked: 30 of 30 at \(d_{out}=8,d_{in}=12,b=4\)), and the Cayley–Neumann map is a local diffeomorphism at \(0\). A skew pair fixing \(W\) would need \(\mathrm{range}\,\Omega_{in}\subseteq\ker W\); for unblocked factors with \(d_{in}\neq d_{out}\) this leaves an \(\mathfrak{so}(|d_{in}-d_{out}|)\) stabiliser, but a generic kernel meets no \(b\)-coordinate block when \(b\le\min(d_{in},d_{out})\) (true for \(b=256,512\)), so the block-diagonal round has trivial gauge.
coord_notes.covariance: A fixed draw imposes a block partition on both sides (\(\Pi\)), but the uniformly redrawn permutations make the law invariant under signed permutations and homotheties on each side: \(\mathbb R^\times B_{d_{out}}\times\mathbb R^\times B_{d_{in}}\) in law, nearest key MonxMon (as LoRA-SB and DARE). The exact-Cayley accumulated orbit is \(CO\times CO\).
coord_notes.merge: \(P_k^\top W_{k-1}R_k^\top\) is a dense matrix of the original shape; merging is part of the schedule.
coord_notes.rebasing: Itself a rebasing scheme. Exact Cayley with redrawn permutations connects the block hypergraphs, so the reach is \(SO(d_{out})\,W_0\,SO(d_{in})\) (Thm V.3(b),(c)), spectrum fixed. With the released Cayley–Neumann factors and \(\lVert Q\rVert_{\rm op}\le2^{1/4}\) every factor is a contraction, so repeated merges shrink every singular value monotonically (Thm V.3, Cor 4).

methods.categorical_reading: POET-X is the multiplicative twin of ReLoRA, run on both sides of the weight: a rebasing scheme whose per-round shape is a two-sided block-orthogonal orbit, with redrawn random permutations doing the work that butterfly factors do in BOFT, connecting the block hypergraph across rounds (Thm V.3(c)). Its spectrum-preservation property holds for exactly orthogonal factors only: with the released Cayley–Neumann map each merge is a contraction in the operating regime, so over many merges the spectrum drifts downward rather than staying fixed.

obstructions.reason: At equal block size b a POET-X round has d = (b-1)(d_in+d_out)/2 skew parameters on both sides, against OFTv2's d_in(b-1)/2 on the input side. OFTv2 maps into a round (freeze P at I, A2), not conversely.
Per stage, P^T W R^T - W has rank up to min(m,n) for generic block-orthogonal factors, while a ReLoRA stage update has rank at most r.

coord_notes.kind: A family over tokens: \(\Delta W(x)=\sum_{e\in\mathrm{TopK}(p(x))}p_e(x)B_eA_e\) on the q/k/v/o (or SSM) projections, with a softmax router; experts are frozen public LoRAs (plug-and-play) or trained.
coord_notes.shape: Token-dependent mixture: no single weight-space image, and top-\(K\) makes the realised functions discontinuous at routing ties.
coord_notes.base_point: The experts are trained or public LoRAs acting from the first routing step, and the softmax weights never vanish together, so no router value gives the frozen function: unpointed (as MoLE). The init of experts trained from scratch is not stated (the repository holds only a README).
coord_notes.gauge: With trained experts (main table) \(GL_r\) on each expert's rank wire, since the scalar gate slides through \(B_eA_e\); router-only training leaves only the softmax translation, a kernel-type redundancy.
coord_notes.covariance: Dense LoRA experts and a dense router transform together: function-level \(GL\times GL\) (routed-mixture convention).
coord_notes.merge: Thm VI.3: token-dependent gates; M1 only for a frozen expert choice.

methods.categorical_reading: LoRA-Mixer is an \(X\)-point of a top-\(K\) LoRA mixture placed on the projections that feed and read out the token mixer, so the routed update passes through attention or the SSM scan in series. Fibrewise it is a rank-\(Er\) LoRA whose blocks are weighted by the routing scores; what is new is the locus and the balance-plus-entropy loss, not the object.

arrows.note: Fibrewise over tokens (per adapted projection), into LoRA_{Er} pointed at h(q_0) (unpointed slice, as PHATGOOSE -> LoRA); smooth away from top-K ties. A renormalisation over the selected set, if used, is absorbed into p_e.

obstructions.reason: MixLoRA routes experts only on the FFN and puts static, input-independent LoRAs on q, k, v, o. LoRA-Mixer's token-dependent updates on the attention projections are therefore generically not MixLoRA realisations (and LoRA-Mixer leaves the FFN frozen).
Token-dependent gates give functions that generically no single weight realises (M-infinity), so they are not in LoraHub's static weight-space image (as for MoLE and X-LoRA).

methods.check_notes: Classified 2026-10-02 from addendum2026b-0 (verified entry; the official repository has no code). Precedents: MoLE (unpointed mixture of trained LoRAs), PHATGOOSE (top-k fibrewise arrow into LoRA_{Nr}). Gauge read for the trained-expert instance of the main table. Independent check 2026-10-02: Coordinates confirmed against MoLE/LoRAMoE/PHATGOOSE precedents (GLxGL by the routed-mixture convention). Fibrewise arrow identity checked (2e-16). Unpointed and GL are instance readings (frozen public experts vs trained experts), as recorded. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: A family over (document, chunk) positions: chunk \(i\) runs with \(W_{down}^{(i)}=W_0+\eta\sum_{j<i}\hat V_{[j]}^\top Z_{[j]}\), written in closed form from the context by the slow modules \(W_{target}\) and a depthwise Conv1D. The outer loop also continually trains every backbone weight, which lies outside the slice; the coordinates describe the inference-time object over the warm-started base.
coord_notes.shape: Different chunks of one document see different weights, so there is no single weight-space image (compared through \(\Phi\)); each fibre is a rank-\(\le(i-1)C\) additive update of \(W_{down}\).
coord_notes.base_point: The Conv1D kernel is zero-initialised, so \(\hat V=0\) and every fast-weight delta vanishes: the frozen function at every position (neutral). There \(W_{target}\) is a zero-gated factor, so only the kernel moves to first order (Lemma II.4).
coord_notes.gauge: \((k_c,\ \text{row }c\text{ of }W_{target})\mapsto(\lambda_ck_c,\ \lambda_c^{-1}\cdot)\) slides through the depthwise convolution: a \(d\)-dimensional torus (\(\eta\) is a fixed hyperparameter).
coord_notes.covariance: The update is a gradient step \(\eta\hat V^\top Z\) whose input side is the box's own activations, which transform as a covector, so it is covariant on the input side only under \(CO(d_{ff})\); the output side is absorbed by the dense trainable \(W_{target}\) (\(GL(d)\)). GLxCO.
coord_notes.merge: A position-gated edit (Thm VI.3(a)): no position-independent weight, and it is reset at every document boundary.

methods.categorical_reading: In-Place TTT is a context-indexed section of 'fine-tune \(W_{down}\) only': a causal fast-weight memory written by one closed-form gradient step per chunk, i.e. a chunked linear-attention branch living inside an existing MLP box. Per (document, chunk) fibre it is a LoRA on \(W_{down}\) whose \(A\) factor is the activations of the earlier chunks and whose \(B\) factor is the generated targets, pointed at \(B=0\) by the zero convolution.

arrows.note: Fibrewise over (document c, chunk index i), into LoRA_{(i-1)C} on W_down (scale 1), pointed at (0,[Z_{[1]};...;Z_{[i-1]}]) because the zero kernel gives V-hat = 0: a T_A-type point whose A_0 is the context's own activations. Uses sum_j V_j^T Z_j = [V_1^T ... V_{i-1}^T][Z_1;...;Z_{i-1}] (checked, 2e-15). Backbone fixed (inference); for long contexts the rank is capped at min(d, d_ff).

obstructions.reason: Doc-to-LoRA generates one static update per document, the same at every position; In-Place TTT's W_down changes from chunk to chunk inside a document, so for generic contexts its position-dependent realised map is not that of any per-document weight.

methods.check_notes: Classified 2026-10-02 from addendum2026b-0 (verified entry, released code ByteDance-Seed/In-Place-TTT). Precedents: PreFT and aLoRA (position-gated F_T, Fun, M-infinity), Doc-to-LoRA (context-indexed LoRA). Doubts: the outer loop is full continual training, so this is a PEFT object only at inference; covariance GLxCO is derived from the gradient-step form of the update (a data frame reading would give 'frame'). Independent check 2026-10-02: Coordinates confirmed (F_T over contexts, neutral at zero kernel, Minf). Block identity sum_j V_j^T Z_j = [V^T][Z] checked (3e-15); the d-dimensional torus (k_c, row c of W_target) confirmed by a function-level Jacobian rank deficit of exactly d (6 at d = 6, no conv bias, as in d^2+5d). GLxCO re-derived: the input side of the update is the box's own activations (CO(d_ff)), the output side is absorbed by the dense W_target. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: Forward map \(\mathrm{id}_\Theta\). The gradient is replaced by \(N\) one-sided Rademacher finite differences sharing one unperturbed loss: compression \(g\mapsto(\langle u_i,g\rangle)_{i\le N}\), anchor \(c\mapsto\tfrac1N\sum_ic_iu_i\), and the step is divided by the loss spread \(\sigma_t\approx\epsilon\lVert\nabla\mathcal L\rVert\) (zeroth-order normalised SGD).
coord_notes.shape: Each step lies in \(\theta_t+\mathrm{span}\{u_1,\dots,u_N\}\) (\(d=N\), resampled every step); MeZO is the line case.
coord_notes.base_point: No reparametrisation; each step is a linear method at its own base.
coord_notes.gauge: None.
coord_notes.covariance: Rademacher probes are invariant in law under signed permutations and homotheties, not under rotations or non-uniform scalings: \(\mathbb R^\times B\) on each side in law, nearest key MonxMon. MeZO's Gaussian probes give \(O(\Theta)\) in law ('frame').
coord_notes.merge: Writes \(\theta\) directly; nothing to merge. The FZOO-prefix variant trains a prefix, which is M\(\infty\).
coord_notes.rebasing: A rebasing scheme of \(N\)-planes resampled every step; the reach is \(\Theta\) (Thm V.3, Cor 6).

methods.categorical_reading: FZOO is MeZO with an \(N\)-dimensional random slice per step instead of a line, and a step length set by the observed loss spread. The change of probe law from Gaussian to Rademacher shows up in the classification: it trades MeZO's rotation covariance in law for signed-permutation covariance, the price of turning the perturbed matrix products into additions.

obstructions.reason: Per step FZOO's slice span{u_1,...,u_N} has d = N > 1 = d(MeZO step line). For N = 1 the step line is a Rademacher line, which a Gaussian line meets only at theta_t almost surely (O1).

Precedents: MeZO, AGZO and ZO-Muon (kind B, Lin per step, schedule; merge null as in batch 11). Classified in full-parameter mode; the prefix mode inherits prefix tuning's coordinates. Independent check 2026-10-02: Coordinates confirmed (MeZO/AGZO precedents; merge null as batch 11). Covariance re-derived: span{g U_i h^-1} has the Rademacher law only for g, h in R^x B (signed permutations times scalars), consistent with DARE's in-law MonxMon; MeZO's Gaussian probes stay 'frame'. O2 holds per step. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: A family over tokens: \(\Delta W(x_t)=\tfrac\alpha r\sum_ip_{t,i}B_iA_i\) on every projection, with Sparsegen routing \(p_t=\arg\min_{p\in\Delta^{E-1}}\lVert p-u_t\rVert^2-\lambda_t\lVert p\rVert^2\) and a per-token \(\lambda_t\) from a shared MLP.
coord_notes.shape: Token-dependent mixture: no single weight-space image. Sparsegen is piecewise linear and continuous, so unlike top-\(K\) the realised functions have no jumps, while weights still vanish exactly on open sets of tokens.
coord_notes.base_point: Every \(B_i\) is zero-initialised in the released code: the frozen function at every token (neutral); gate and \(\lambda\)-MLP get no first-order gradient (zero gate).
coord_notes.gauge: \(GL_r\) on each expert's rank wire (the routing weight slides through \(B_iA_i\)); the simplex projection is invariant under \(u\mapsto u+c\mathbf 1\), so the bias-free gate also has the kernel-type shift \(W_{gate}\mapsto W_{gate}+\mathbf 1v^\top\).
coord_notes.covariance: Dense LoRA experts and a dense gate: function-level \(GL\times GL\).
coord_notes.merge: Token-dependent \(p_t\) (Thm VI.3).

methods.categorical_reading: LD-MoLE is a LoRA mixture whose router is a Euclidean projection onto the simplex with a learned quadratic bonus, so the number of active experts is a per-token output and the routing is continuous. Fibrewise it is LoRA\(_{Er}\) with token-dependent block weights, pointed at \(B=0\).

arrows.note: Fibrewise over tokens, into LoRA_{Er} with scale s, pointed at (0,[A_1^0;...;A_E^0]) since every B_i starts at 0 (as HydraLoRA -> LoRA). h_x is continuous and piecewise smooth (Sparsegen's support changes across hyperplanes).

obstructions.reason: LoRAMoE's softmax weights are strictly positive and its experts sit on the FFN only. LD-MoLE's Sparsegen weights vanish exactly on open sets of tokens and its experts also edit the attention projections; for generic experts (linearly independent B_iA_ix) equal realised functions would force equal weights, so its sparse routings are not LoRAMoE realisations.

methods.check_notes: Classified 2026-10-02 from addendum2026b-0 (verified entry, released code eshentw/LD-MoLE with a vendored PEFT). Precedents: LoRAMoE and HydraLoRA (neutral routed mixtures, fibrewise arrow into LoRA). The shift invariance of Sparsegen was re-derived from the simplex constraint. Independent check 2026-10-02: Coordinates confirmed (LoRAMoE/HydraLoRA precedents). Checked: Sparsegen output on the simplex, invariant under u -> u + c1 (2e-16); fibrewise arrow into LoRA_{Er} with scale s (4e-16). The LoRAMoE obstruction stands on locus (FFN-only vs all projections) and on exact zeros vs positive softmax weights. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: LoRA's \(\rho=W_0+\alpha\sum_kb_ka_k^\top\) (coefficient \(\gamma/r=\alpha\) instead of \(\alpha/r\)), trained by cyclic block-coordinate two-point zeroth-order queries on one rank-1 atom \((b_k,a_k)\) at a time; oracle and schedule are trained-method data.
coord_notes.shape: LoRA's cone \(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\).
coord_notes.base_point: \(B_0=0\) with random \(A_0\) (App. B.1): the \(\mathrm T_A\) apex.
coord_notes.gauge: \(GL_r\) on \(\rho\). The atomwise oracle respects only the atom torus \((b_k,a_k)\mapsto(cb_k,a_k/c)\) with the cyclic order fixed, and its Gaussian probes are not torus-invariant either.
coord_notes.covariance: LoRA's basis-free cone (the Gaussian probes in \(b,a\) are \(O\)-invariant in law).
coord_notes.merge: A plain \(\alpha BA\).

methods.categorical_reading: AR1-ZO is LoRA rescaled by \(r\) and trained one rank-1 atom at a time from two forward passes; as an object it is LoRA, by an isomorphism of the rsLoRA kind. Its content is in the trained-method data: each query has dimension \(d_{in}+d_{out}\) and the coefficient \(\alpha\) keeps the finite-difference signal independent of the rank, so rank becomes coverage rather than query dimension.

arrows.note: Isomorphism onto LoRA_r with scale s (as rsLoRA = LoRA), pointed: B_0 = 0 maps to 0.

obstructions.reason: Over a cycle every atom moves in both factors, so d(AR1-ZO) = r(m+n-r) > mr = d(LoRA-FA).

methods.check_notes: Classified 2026-10-02 from addendum2026b-1 (verified entry; no code). Precedents: rsLoRA (same object up to scale) and Stable-LoRA / LoRA-RITE (an update rule on LoRA's object, h = id). Independent check 2026-10-02: Coordinates confirmed (object = LoRA with coefficient alpha). Arrow h = (alpha/s B, A) is a pointed isomorphism by inspection; O2 vs LoRA-FA: r(m+n-r) > mr for n > r. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: Post hoc and data-free: every output factor is left-multiplied by \(S=I+U\,\mathrm{diag}(\alpha-\mathbf 1)U^\top\) (\(U\) from the SVD of \([B_1,\dots,B_T]\), \(\alpha_j=1/(1+(T-1)s_j)\)); a base rule \(\mathcal M\) merges the \(SB_tA_t\) and \(\gamma\) restores the mean source norm.
coord_notes.shape: No tunable coefficient (\(\alpha\), \(S\) and \(\gamma\) are closed-form, and \(\gamma\) cancels any overall merge weight): a single point (post-hoc convention).
coord_notes.base_point: A single point, generically \(\neq\theta_0\); for \(T=1\) under task arithmetic it returns the adapter \(B_1A_1\) itself.
coord_notes.gauge: No coefficient family. Note: \(S\) depends on \(\sum_tB_tB_t^\top\), not on the products, so Pico is invariant under per-adapter \(O(r)\) gauges but not under \(GL_r\) (checked: output change \(5\times10^{-15}\) under an orthogonal gauge, 0.37 under a generic one): a factor-level rule (Prop V.4(a)).
coord_notes.covariance: \(S\) is built from an SVD of the stacked \(B_t\) and transports under \(g\in CO(d_{out})\) (\(S\mapsto gSg^{-1}\)); \(A_t\) is untouched, but the norm-restoring \(\gamma\) is a ratio of Frobenius norms, which is invariant only under \(CO\) on each side. With task arithmetic inside the group is exactly \(CO(d_{out})\times CO(d_{in})\): OxO (checked: \(2\times10^{-15}\) under \(CO\times CO\), \(4\times10^{-2}\) under \(CO\times GL\), \(0.35\) under a generic output \(GL\)). TIES or TSV-M inside cut it further.
coord_notes.merge: One additive delta per layer, of rank \(\le Tr\) under task arithmetic.

methods.categorical_reading: Pico is a spectral reweighting of the shared output space before merging: under task arithmetic it is the post-merge map \(\Delta W\mapsto\gamma S\Delta W\), so its effect on nonlinear mergers comes only from applying \(S\) first. Because \(S\) is read off the \(B\) factors rather than the adapters, it depends on how each LoRA's scale is split between \(B\) and \(A\), which is what the design rule 'combine on products, or after a joint gauge fixing' (Prop V.4) warns about.

arrows.note: Pico-TA instance: the merged point is a point of LoRA_{Tr}'s image (unpointed slice, LoRA pointed at h(*)), as model soups into task arithmetic.

obstructions.reason: For T >= 2 and generic adapters, gamma S sum_t B_tA_t leaves span{B_tA_t}: S mixes the shared output directions, so Pico-TA is not a reweighted task arithmetic.

methods.check_notes: Classified 2026-10-02 from addendum2026b-1 (verified entry; no code). Precedents: model soups (closed-form P point, shape and gauge null) and Compress-then-Merge / KnOTS (SVD frames, OxO). The O(r)-only gauge invariance was checked numerically (T = 3, r = 2). Independent check 2026-10-02: Shape/gauge null and unpointed match the model-soups/OrthoMerge convention. Checked: arrow into LoRA_{Tr} (1e-15); O(r) gauge invariance 3e-15 vs 0.76 under GL_r; Pico-TA leaves span{B_tA_t} (relative residual 0.15), so the TA obstruction holds. Changed: covariance note; the key OxO was right but the group is CO x CO, not CO x GL, because gamma is a ratio of Frobenius norms (numerically 2e-15 under CO x CO, 4e-2 under CO x GL).

coord_notes.kind: Additive \(W_0+c\,P_{out}CP_{in}^\top\) (\(c=\alpha/\sqrt{d_{out}d_{in}}\)) with fixed Parseval fusion frames, a block-diagonal core \(C\) and a random support \(\Omega\) shared by all layers; only \(C_\Omega\) trains.
coord_notes.shape: Linear in \(C_\Omega\), \(d=n_c\). Every reported run has \(k\rho=d\), so the frames are square orthogonal matrices (at \(\rho=2\) the realified DFT basis) and \(\Delta W\) is a coordinate mask in that two-sided frame.
coord_notes.base_point: With init_std 0 (the instruction-tuning scripts) \(C=0\): regular. The GLUE scripts keep the default \(\mathcal N(0,1)\) coefficients, a pointing defect as for HF's FourierFT default.
coord_notes.gauge: None: orthogonal frames make \(C\mapsto P_{out}CP_{in}^\top\) injective.
coord_notes.covariance: The frames depend only on \((d,\rho)\) and impose a DFT-type cyclic order on both sides, and the block structure a partition: \(\Pi\), as FourierFT.

methods.categorical_reading: FrameFT is a SHiRA-type coordinate mask transported by a fixed two-sided frame \(X\mapsto P_{out}XP_{in}^\top\), which in all reported settings is a realified DFT on both sides; the transport is \(\theta_0\)-independent, unlike SVFT's. It is a FourierFT relative that couples each output frequency block only with the matching input block, through a dense \(\rho\times\rho\) core.

arrows.note: J = columns of C met by Omega; into LoRA-FA_{|J|} with the frozen frame rows A_0 (LoRA-FA scale 1; otherwise divide h by it), pointed at 0 (as SVFT -> LoRA-FA). Checked numerically (6e-17).

obstructions.reason: FourierFT's image is spanned by a few real 2-D cosine patterns cos(2 pi (j x/d_out + l y/d_in)) at sampled frequencies (rank 2 each, point-symmetric); FrameFT's atoms are rank-one products of realified (d/2)-point DFT vectors on each side, block-diagonal in frequency. A rank-one atom would need both (j,l) and (j,-l) sampled at matching frequencies, so for generic supports Im FrameFT is not contained in Im FourierFT.
The maximum rank reaches n_c (block-diagonal core), far above r at matched budgets.

methods.categorical_reading: PMT turns prefix tuning's renormalised prompt contribution into an ungated kernel-feature memory: by Thm VI.5(b) a prefix rescales content attention by \(1-\lambda_q\), while PMT keeps the content path at weight 1 and adds \(M^\top\phi(q)\). That buys a neutral point (as LLaMA-Adapter's gate does) and makes the method a parallel branch around attention whose down-projection is the frozen \(W_Q\), whose activation is \(\phi\) (elu or gelu) and whose up-projection is \(W_O\) times a trained block-diagonal map. Because \(\phi\) is not ReLU, this is not the catalogued (ReLU) parallel adapter, so no arrow into it is recorded.

obstructions.reason: f lies in Im PMT (at M = 0) but not in Im prefix tuning, which is unpointed (Thm VI.5(f)); moreover a prefix multiplies content attention by 1 - lambda_q, which PMT never does.
For generic M the branch is non-affine in the input (elu or gelu), while every LoRA setting keeps the attention projections linear, so no weight-space LoRA realises it (Thm VI.3(c)).

The catalogued parallel adapter is He et al.'s ReLU bottleneck, whose branch U ReLU(D x) is piecewise linear in its input. PMT's branch sum_h W_O^(h) M_h^T phi(W_Q^(h) x) with phi = elu or gelu is real-analytic and non-affine on open sets of (normalised) inputs, so for generic M it equals no finite ReLU branch: Im PMT is not inside Im PA. PMT factors only through a phi-activated parallel branch with a frozen down-projection W_Q, which is not a catalogued object (the parallel-adapter entry excludes GELU-bottleneck arrows for the same reason).

coord_notes.kind: QLoRA-type: a frozen NVFP4 residual \(Q(R)\), a frozen high-precision rank-\(k\) stabiliser \(L_{stab}=L_1L_2\) (SVDQuant) and a trainable LoRA \(BA\), computed in W4A4G4. The 4-bit activation quantiser changes the network itself (\(f\mapsto\tilde f\)), so the slice is over the quantised architecture.
coord_notes.shape: \(Q(R)+L_{stab}+\mathcal M_{\le r}\): LoRA's cone at the quantised base \(\kappa'\theta_0=Q(R)+L_{stab}\) (Prop V.2(a)).
coord_notes.base_point: Defect \(e=Q(R)+L_{stab}-W_0\), the quantisation error of the SVDQuant residual, on top of the activation quantisation; a zero-factor LoRA start is assumed (not stated).
coord_notes.covariance: The NVFP4 grid with \(16\times16\) block scales lives in the standard basis: Mon×Mon (grid), as QLoRA.
coord_notes.merge: Folding \(BA\) into \(Q(R)\) leaves the 4-bit type (or requantises lossily); concatenation into the high-precision branch, \([L_1\ B][L_2;A]\), is exact but raises its rank from \(k\) to \(k+r\). Coded Mq.

methods.categorical_reading: FourTune is QLoRA over a different base change: the quantiser is SVDQuant's split into a high-precision low-rank part plus a 4-bit residual, kept frozen during training, and both passes run in 4-bit arithmetic. As an object it is LoRA at the translate \(Q(R)+L_{stab}\). The stabiliser and the adapter have the same algebraic form, which is why the trained LoRA can be absorbed exactly into the low-rank branch, but not into the 4-bit weight.

obstructions.reason: Different quantisers give different translates of the same cone: Q(R) + L_stab and NF4(W_0) differ by a generically full-rank matrix, and c + M_{<=r} lies in c' + M_{<=r} only if c = c' (proof of Thm II.2(a)). The activation quantisers differ as well (A4 against A16).
rho(q_0) = Q(R) + L_stab != theta_0, and theta_0 is not in the image unless rank e <= r (Prop V.2(a)): no pointed arrow.

coord_notes.kind: Post hoc and training-free: a task vector \(\tau_A\) computed at base \(\theta_A\) is masked by sign agreement with the target's anti-gradient, \(m_i=\mathbb 1\{\mathrm{sign}\,\tau_{A,i}=\hat s_i\}\) (majority vote over a few labelled samples), and added to a new base \(\theta_B\) with a validation-tuned \(\alpha\).
coord_notes.shape: The coefficient line \(\theta_B+\alpha(m\odot\tau_A)\), \(d=1\).
coord_notes.base_point: \(\alpha=0\) returns \(\theta_B\); the slice is the one at the new base.
coord_notes.gauge: None.
coord_notes.covariance: The mask compares the signs of a vector and a covector: under \(\theta\mapsto D\theta\) with \(D\) invertible diagonal, \(\tau\mapsto D\tau\) and \(g\mapsto D^{-1}g\), so every sign agreement survives; permutations too, rotations not. Exactly \(\mathrm{Mon}_N\) (magnitude-free, larger than TIES's \(\mathbb R^\times B_N\)): MonxMon.
coord_notes.merge: One additive delta on \(\theta_B\).
coord_notes.rebasing: Idempotent with the mask frozen; recomputing the mask at the merged point is a new transport.

methods.categorical_reading: GradFix is a base-change map for task vectors: a displacement measured at \(\theta_A\) is projected, coordinate by coordinate, onto the descent orthant \(\{\delta:\delta_ig_i\le0\}\) of the loss at \(\theta_B\), which is exactly its first-order guarantee. Being coordinatewise it is monomial-natural, not rotation-natural, and it would turn a LoRA task vector into a masked dense matrix.

arrows.note: Per transport, over the base theta_B: the line lies in FISH with mask M = supp(m), pointed at 0 (as Sparse Memory Finetuning -> FISH).

obstructions.reason: When the mask keeps part but not all of the support of tau_A, m (.) tau_A is not a multiple of tau_A, so the line differs from task arithmetic's theta_B + lambda tau_A (which stays near zero-shot across bases, as the paper reports).

methods.check_notes: Classified 2026-10-02 from addendum2026b-1 (verified entry, code fillo-rinaldi/GradFix). Precedents: task arithmetic and DARE (P, Lin, coefficient line; DARE's Mon_N covariance). coord_notes.kind: A family over per-layer quantisation configurations \(\mathbf C\) (\(432^N\) of them): \(\Delta W_i(\mathbf C)=L_{1,i}(I_r+U_\theta(Q_i))L_{2,i}\) on \(\widetilde W_{\mathbf C}\), with the \(r\times r\) core generated by one hypernetwork from configuration, module-type and block embeddings. Read in the released instance, where one LoRA pair is trained jointly with \(\theta\) and shared by all configurations.
coord_notes.shape: Each fibre lies in \(\widetilde W_{\mathbf C}+\mathcal M_{\le r}\) and starts at a rank-\(r\) point: LoRA's cone translated to a quantised apex (Cone*, as LQ-LoRA). With the paper's frozen factors (Eq. 3) a fibre is only the \(r^2\)-dimensional core window \(\widetilde W_{\mathbf C}+L_1\mathbb R^{r\times r}L_2\) (Lin).
coord_notes.base_point: \(I_r+U_\theta\approx I_r\) at init and \(L_1L_2=\mathrm{SVD}_r(W_0-\widetilde W_{\mathbf C})\): pointed up to the attained residual (an approximate section, Prop V.2(c)). In the code the shared pair comes from one configuration's residual, so the other configurations start with a larger defect.
coord_notes.gauge: \((L_1,L_2)\mapsto(L_1G^{-1},GL_2)\) with the core conjugated, \(C\mapsto GCG^{-1}\) (which keeps the identity term), absorbed by the mapper's linear last layer; plus the slide of \(\gamma\) against that layer. Coded GL.
coord_notes.covariance: NormalFloat grids and block sizes live in the standard basis: Mon×Mon (grid), as QLoRA and LQ-LoRA.
coord_notes.merge: For a fixed configuration the update is a static rank-\(r\) matrix, but folding it into \(\widetilde W_{\mathbf C}\) needs dequantisation (requantising changes the configuration), and the mapper must stay to serve the others.
coord_notes.rebasing: Undefined for a family whose fibre changes with the configuration.

methods.categorical_reading: CoA-LoRA is a section of LQ-LoRA over the space of per-layer quantisation configurations: one hypernetwork turns each configuration into an \(r\times r\) move inside a fixed pair of column and row spaces, as NaRA does over noise levels. Every fibre lives in a different translate of LoRA's cone, one per quantised base, and is pointed only up to that configuration's attained residual.

arrows.note: Fibrewise over configurations, per layer, into LQ-LoRA over the quantised base W~_C, pointed at h_C(q_0) (approximately (L_1, L_2), since the mapper's last layer starts at N(0,1e-6)). This is LQ-LoRA's own start when W~_C and the factors come from the same low-rank-plus-quantised split at that configuration.

obstructions.reason: A rank-r start that compensates the quantisation error (a smooth point over W~_C) against QLoRA's apex at kappa theta_0, with different apexes as well (as LQ-LoRA).

coord_notes.kind: Action type on a ternary checkpoint: \(\mathrm{diag}(s)\big(W_{tern}\odot(A\otimes B)\big)\), with ternary Kronecker factors obtained by thresholding real proxies (straight-through estimator).
coord_notes.shape: The orbit of \(\theta_0\) under the Hadamard monoid of ternary Kronecker masks \(\{A\otimes B\}\subset\{-1,0,1\}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}}\): a finite set (\(d=0\)), as Piggyback's Boolean orbit. The STE surrogate treats it as \(W\odot(\bar A\otimes\bar B)\), a Hadamard-transported rank-one Kronecker cone; that relaxation is training data, not \(\rho\).
coord_notes.base_point: All-ones factors (or the sign-compensated balanced init) give \(\theta_0\) exactly; with \(d=0\), \(\dim S_1=0=d\): regular trivially (Piggyback). (In the STE relaxation the all-ones point is also regular: \(\dim S_1=p_1q_1+p_2q_2-1\).)
coord_notes.gauge: \(\rho\) depends on the proxies only through \(\mathrm{Tern}(\bar A),\mathrm{Tern}(\bar B)\), whose thresholds are mean-relative: the generic fibre is an open code cell of full dimension \(p_1q_1+p_2q_2\). Its only exhibited linear symmetries are the positive scalings of each factor (Tern is scale-invariant) and the sign slide \((A,B)\mapsto(-A,-B)\); per-entry positive scalings, which give Piggyback's torus, change the cell (checked: 99.95% of random ones), so the fibre is not a torus orbit: non-linear, as L4Q's code cells.
coord_notes.covariance: Hadamard structure (Mon×Mon) composed with an imposed Kronecker reshape, which breaks neuron permutations: \(\Pi\), as LoKr and KronA.
coord_notes.merge: \(W_{tern}\odot(A\otimes B)\) is again ternary with unchanged scales: the exact merge stays in the quantised type (the opposite of Mq).
coord_notes.rebasing: \((A\otimes B)\odot(C\otimes D)=(A\odot C)\otimes(B\odot D)\) (checked), so ternary Kronecker masks form a submonoid: idempotent. Zeros can never be reactivated.

methods.categorical_reading: Ternary adaptation replaces the additive update, which leaves the ternary grid, by a monoid action that preserves it. The merge is type-preserving by construction, so the quantised-type obstruction of Prop V.2(d) disappears, and so does any gain from merge-and-restart, since the masks form a submonoid. The Kronecker constraint is what makes a sign-flip mask cheap, and it is also an imposed structure.

obstructions.reason: Piggyback's masks are {0,1}-valued, so its image keeps every sign of W_0; a ternary mask flips the signs of nonzero weights (about 26% of weights flip in the paper's transition analysis).

The ternary update diag(s)(W_tern (.) (A (x) B - 11^T)) carries the generic zero/sign pattern of W_tern, so its Van Loan-Pitsianis rearrangement has rank > 1 (checked: 6 for the same split, 4 for another), while LoKr's update C (x) BA is a single Kronecker term (rearrangement rank 1). Hence Im ternary is not inside Im LoKr. (Conversely LoKr can create entries where W_0 is zero, which the zero-locking ternary action cannot.)

coord_notes.kind: Post hoc, at test time: \(W^l(B)=W_0^l+\lambda^l\sum_iU_i^l\,\mathrm{diag}(B_i^l)\,\Sigma_i^lV_i^{l\top}\) with binary keep/prune masks on every singular triplet and one coefficient per layer, fitted by entropy minimisation on unlabeled test inputs (straight-through estimator).
coord_notes.shape: For each mask a layer-wise line; the coefficient family is the finite union of these lines through \(\theta_0\), a cone (a union of linear spaces, as Diff pruning).
coord_notes.base_point: Optimisation starts at the base merger (for TA: \(B=\mathbf 1\), \(\lambda=0.3\)), not at \(\theta_0\): a defect, as AdaMerging. \(B=0\) or \(\lambda=0\) returns \(W_0\).
coord_notes.gauge: The mask logits enter only through \(B_{i,r}=\mathbb 1[\tilde b_{i,r}\ge0]\) (\(\sigma(\tilde b/T)\ge0.5\)), so the generic fibre is an open orthant cell, exactly an orbit of the positive torus \(\tilde b\mapsto c\odot\tilde b\) (fibre dimension \(T\min(d_{out},d_{in})\) per matrix), as for Piggyback and Masking; for a fixed mask \(\lambda\mapsto\lambda D(B)\) is injective when \(D(B)\neq0\).
coord_notes.covariance: Per-task singular frames are \(CO\times CO\)-covariant and masking whole triplets commutes with them (TA base): OxO, as KnOTS and TSV-M.
coord_notes.merge: One static weight set after adaptation.
coord_notes.rebasing: With frames frozen the shape is closed under scaling, so \(R_\infty=W_0+\mathrm{span}\{\sigma_{i,k}u_{i,k}v_{i,k}^\top\}\) per layer (Thm V.3(a)).

methods.categorical_reading: AdaRank enlarges task arithmetic's coefficient line to a union of lines indexed by subsets of singular triplets: top-\(k\) truncation (SVD merging, TSV-M) and full task arithmetic are two of its points, and test-time entropy picks another. It is a spectral-coordinate analogue of DARE and TIES, with a learned mask instead of a random or magnitude-based one.

obstructions.reason: For a mask that keeps part of a task's spectrum, sum_i U_i diag(B_i) Sigma_i V_i^T leaves span{tau_i^l}, while AdaMerging's family stays in that span (B = 1 gives its layer-constant points).
TIES trims and elects signs coordinatewise in weight coordinates; AdaRank keeps or prunes whole singular triplets. Their merged vectors differ generically.

The mask logits enter only through 1[b >= 0], so the generic fibre is an open orthant cell, an orbit of the positive torus, exactly the Piggyback/Masking reading. Checked: a partial-mask merge leaves span{tau_i} (residual 0.73), so the AdaMerging obstruction holds; TIES obstruction stands.

coord_notes.kind: One LoRA pair over a task stream: before task \(i\ge2\), \(A\) is replaced by \(Q_i^\top=R_i^{-\top}A_{ft,i-1}\) (orthonormal rows) and \(B\) by \(B_{ft,i-1}\); after training, \(A\) is overwritten and only \(B\) is averaged with weight \(1/\sqrt i\). \(W_0\) is never merged into.
coord_notes.shape: Every stage and every deployed model lies in LoRA's cone \(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\).
coord_notes.base_point: Task 1 is the \(\mathrm T_A\) apex. Each later stage starts at \(W_0+B_{ft,i-1}R_i^{-\top}A_{ft,i-1}\), which differs by design from the deployed model \(W_0+B^{i-1}_{merge}A_{ft,i-1}\) (no compensating \(R_i^\top\), and the raw rather than the merged \(B\)): a pointing defect.
coord_notes.gauge: \(GL_r\) on \(\rho\). The QR step fixes the gauge of \(A\) on the Stiefel slice without the compensating move on \(B\), and the \(B\)-only average pairs past \(B\)'s with the latest \(A\): a factor-level rule, exact only to the extent that all \(A\)'s share one row space (Prop V.4(b)).
coord_notes.covariance: The image is LoRA's basis-free cone; the QR normalisation is only \(O(d_{in})\)-equivariant.
coord_notes.merge: The deployed \(B^t_{merge}A^t_{merge}\) is one LoRA and fuses.
coord_notes.rebasing: Not a rebasing scheme: the base \(W_0\) is never re-pointed and every stage has the same shape, so the stream's own reach stays \(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\) for every length (unlike O-LoRA's \(\mathcal M_{\le Tr}\)). The axis value is that of the shape: LoRA's cone, closed under scaling, so merge-and-restart gives \(\to\Theta\) (Thm V.3(a)).

methods.categorical_reading: SLAO is continual merging carried out inside one LoRA: the stream is a schedule of re-pointings within a fixed cone, each a non-gauge move (QR rebasing of \(A\), warm start of \(B\)) followed by a factor-level average of \(B\). It works to the extent that every \(A\) descends from one row space, which is the shared-factor condition under which factor-wise merging is exact (Prop V.4(b)). Memory stays constant because the rank never grows.

arrows.note: First stage: a pointed isomorphism onto LoRA_r at (0, A_0). Later stages start at W_0 + B_{ft,i-1}Q_i^T and map only by a weak morphism (LoRA re-pointed at that start).

obstructions.reason: Each SLAO stage trains both factors, d = r(m+n-r), while an InfLoRA stage is LoRA-FA(A_t) with d = rm.

coord_notes.kind: Post hoc and gradient-free: the instruction task vector \(\Delta_I=\theta_I-\theta_B\) is right-projected off the span of each module's inputs at the thinking markers, rescaled per head in closed form, and added to a different model \(\theta_R\) with a grid-searched \(\lambda\).
coord_notes.shape: The coefficient line \(\theta_R+\lambda\bigoplus_k\alpha^k_\star\Delta_I^{\perp,k}\) (\(\alpha_\star\) closed-form, \(\lambda\) tuned): \(d=1\).
coord_notes.base_point: \(\lambda=0\) returns \(\theta_R\); for 1.5B and 7B, \(\theta_R\) is not even fine-tuned from \(\theta_B\), so the task vector is transported across bases.
coord_notes.gauge: None.
coord_notes.covariance: The orthogonal (or ridge) projector \(I-H(H^\top H)^+H^\top\) acts on the input side and is covariant under \(CO(d_{in})\) (\(H\mapsto hH\)); left multiplication leaves the output side free; Stage 2's per-head coefficients follow the network's own head partition. GLxCO.
coord_notes.merge: One static weight set.

methods.categorical_reading: RAIN-Merging is task arithmetic across bases with a null-space constraint: Stage 1 makes the added vector vanish on the thinking-marker activations, so the merged modules compute exactly as \(\theta_R\) there, and Stage 2 is a closed-form per-head reweighting. The family is still a line through \(\theta_R\) along one projected, block-rescaled vector, so the content is in the choice of vector, not in the family.

obstructions.reason: The projected, per-head rescaled vector generically leaves span{Delta_I}: Delta_I(I - P_H) is a multiple of Delta_I only if Delta_I already annihilates the marker inputs.

coord_notes.kind: A family over tokens: frozen retrieved LoRAs are split into rank-one experts \(b_ma_m^\top\) and recombined per token, \(\Delta W(x)=\widehat B\,\mathrm{diag}(\tilde g(x))\,\widehat A\), with a softmax router, top-\(q_j\) masking and a budget allocator (EEQA); only the routers train (federated).

The rank-one split depends on each library LoRA's factorisation, so MoRE is invariant under per-LoRA monomial changes \(\mathrm{Mon}_r\) but not under its \(GL_r\) gauge.

coord_notes.merge: Token-dependent gates (Thm VI.3); constant gates would give the static \(\widehat B\,\mathrm{diag}(c)\,\widehat A\).

methods.categorical_reading: MoRE is MoLE moved down from whole LoRAs to their rank-one atoms: per token it is a point of LoRA\(_M\) with frozen concatenated factors and a routed diagonal core, which avoids the cross terms of factor averaging. Splitting a LoRA into atoms is not a function of its product \(BA\), so the expert pool, and hence the method, depends on the representative in which each library LoRA was stored.

arrows.note: Fibrewise over tokens, into LoRA_M (M = sum_n r_n) with A frozen at A-hat, pointed at h(q_0) (unpointed slice); smooth away from top-K ties.

coord_notes.covariance: Experts, scaling gate and rotation gate read the input densely: function-level \(GL\times GL\).
coord_notes.merge: Scales, angles and rotation planes change per token (Thm VI.3).

methods.categorical_reading: RotMoLE gives each routed LoRA expert an input-dependent rotation inside its rank space. A constant rotation there would be absorbed by LoRA's \(GL_r\) gauge and add nothing; a token-dependent one cannot be absorbed, and because it uses the Euclidean structure of the code space it cuts the residual gauge down to the similarity group.

arrows.note: Fibrewise over tokens, into LoRA_{nr} pointed at (0,[A_1^0;...;A_n^0]), since every B_i starts at 0. Smooth away from routing ties and from A_ix = 0 (r > 2).

MixLoRA's routed experts also sit on the FFN, RotMoLE's on q, k, v, o.

MixLoRA obstruction stands (non-differentiable on {A_i x = 0}; different locus). No changes.

coord_notes.kind: A rebasing scheme inside one run: every step (ScaLoRA) or every \(I\) steps (ScaLoRA-I) the product is re-split \(W_t=\widetilde W_0^{(t)}+\widetilde B_t\widetilde A_t\) with \(\widetilde B=B\,\mathrm{diag}(\alpha)\), \(\widetilde A=\mathrm{diag}(\beta)A\); the complement \(B\,\mathrm{diag}(\mathbf 1-\alpha\circ\beta)A\) is merged into the frozen weight and Adam's moments are rescaled in closed form.
coord_notes.shape: Each stage is LoRA's cone translated to \(\widetilde W_0^{(t)}\) and started at the rank-\(r\) point \(\widetilde B_t\widetilde A_t\): a translated cone (Cone*), unlike ReLoRA's restarts at the apex.
coord_notes.base_point: The re-split is function-preserving and compensated, so every stage starts at a smooth point (stratum S) wherever \(\alpha\circ\beta\) has no zero entry; stage 0 is LoRA's zero-factor apex.
coord_notes.gauge: \(GL_r\) per stage. Where \(\alpha\circ\beta>0\), write \((\alpha,\beta)=(c\circ s,\ c^{-1}\circ s)\): a torus gauge move \(c\) (no effect on \(W\), but on the next Adam step) followed by a per-direction rescaling \(s^{\circ2}\) whose complement is merged.
coord_notes.covariance: The reach is that of a LoRA rebasing scheme, basis-free; the choice of \((\alpha,\beta)\) uses Frobenius norms (\(O\times O\)) and the moment transport is equivariant only under the torus.
coord_notes.merge: Merged at every re-split; the deliverable is the dense \(W_T\).
coord_notes.rebasing: Itself a rebasing scheme with reach \(\Theta\) (Thm V.3, Cor 1); the paper measures cumulative ranks of 54 at \(r=4\) and over a thousand at \(r=8\).

methods.categorical_reading: ScaLoRA is ReLoRA without restarts: every step is a merge-and-restart, but the restart lands at a rescaled copy of the current factors, a split smooth point, instead of the apex, and the optimizer state is transported instead of reset. Its one degree of freedom per re-split is a diagonal rescaling, the largest family under which Adam's moments transform in closed form, chosen to best match a full fine-tuning step.

arrows.note: Per stage: the stage over W~_0^{(t)} = W_t - B~_tA~_t factors through LoRA_{2r} on the pre-split weight W_t (Thm II.1 conversion), at the degenerate pointing ([B~_t,-B~_t],[A~_t;A~_t]).

obstructions.reason: Per stage ScaLoRA restarts at a smooth split point and ReLoRA at the apex (B = 0): different strata, so the stage images are incomparable at equal rank (Thm II.2(d)).
After K re-splits ScaLoRA's cumulative update can reach rank min((K+1)r, m, n) (measured: 54 at r = 4), while Delta-LoRA's total update has rank at most 2r.

coord_notes.kind: LoRA's \(\rho=W_0+BA\). The optimizer preconditions the full gradient in matrix space (AdamS, LRACS), projects the direction onto \(T_{BA}\mathcal M_r\) through an \(r\times r\) Sylvester solve and lifts it horizontally to the factors.
coord_notes.shape: LoRA's cone.
coord_notes.base_point: Read at LoRA's \(\mathrm T_A\) apex. The lift needs \((B^\top B)^{-1}\), so it is undefined at \(B=0\) (as undamped scaled GD); the start actually used is not shown in the available material (poster only).
coord_notes.gauge: \(GL_r\), all of it respected: the step is equivariant under \((B,A)\mapsto(BR,R^{-1}A)\) with \(K\mapsto R^\top KR^{-\top}\), and the optimizer state lives in matrix space (the poster's Theorem 1; class (c) of Thm III.12).
coord_notes.covariance: The image is LoRA's basis-free cone; the matrix-space Adam preconditioner is coordinatewise, so the trajectory is only monomially covariant.
coord_notes.merge: A standard \(BA\).

methods.categorical_reading: LoRA-S is LoRA with a descending optimizer: any matrix-space preconditioner, followed by the orthogonal projection onto the fixed-rank tangent space and a horizontal lift. A zero Sylvester matrix gives scaled GD (Riemannian-preconditioned LoRA) and \(K=\epsilon I\) gives decoupled weight decay on both factors; as an object it is LoRA.

arrows.note: Same object; only the update rule (trained-method data) differs, as for LoRA-Pro and Riemannian-preconditioned LoRA.

methods.categorical_reading: DiaBlo is a fixed-mask selective method whose mask is block-diagonal: the linear shape between MELoRA (each block factored at rank \(r/N\)) and full fine-tuning. Linearity is the point: it has no gauge and no apex, so the zero-factor stall and initialisation sensitivity of bilinear adapters do not arise, at the price of an imposed coordinate partition.

The block support is one fixed coordinate set, a stratum of Diff pruning's learned-support cone (within the L0 budget when k >= d_in d_out / N), as SMT -> Diff pruning.

At equal N, d(DiaBlo) = d_in d_out / N exceeds MELoRA's sum over blocks of (r/N)(d_in/N + d_out/N - r/N); MELoRA maps into DiaBlo (factor each block), not conversely.

The clipping belongs to the trained-method data; it biases the estimate towards a shrinkage along the gradient rather than leaving it unbiased.

coord_notes.base_point: The meta-learned start \(\theta_{adapter}\) is generically nonzero, so the model differs from the base before test-time training: a defect.

coord_notes.covariance: Fibrewise LoRA's basis-free cone.

methods.categorical_reading: PERK is a gradient-based amortiser: where Doc-to-LoRA or SHINE map a context to a LoRA by one hypernetwork pass, PERK maps it by four unrolled optimizer steps from a learned start. Because Adam sees only a finite shadow of the gauge, the meta-learned quantity includes a choice of factorisation, which is part of what the four steps can write.

arrows.note: Fibrewise over contexts, into LoRA_r (rsLoRA scale absorbed) pointed at h_c(q_0) (defect): the unrolled inner loop is an explicit map, smooth for Adam with eps > 0.

obstructions.reason: PERK writes rank-256 updates into every linear module (the top 4 layers at 7B/8B), Doc-to-LoRA only into the MLP down-projections; a PERK context with a nonzero attention update is outside Doc-to-LoRA's image.

Independent check 2026-10-02: Coordinates confirmed (Doc-to-LoRA/SHINE precedents). The fibrewise arrow (unrolled inner loop as an explicit map) and the Doc-to-LoRA obstruction (attention updates outside D2L's down-projection image) stand. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: A family over inputs: VPT-Deep prompts regenerated at every block from that block's own patch tokens, \(p^{(l)}_j=g\big(\sum_k\alpha^{(l)}_{j,k}(F^{(l)}*X^{(l)}_{img})_k\big)\), with a channel-shared kernel, token pooling and one shared bottleneck MLP (residual in the code).
coord_notes.shape: Function-level: input-dependent extra keys and values at every block.
coord_notes.base_point: Zero-initialised generators give zero prompt tokens, which pre-LN maps to the LayerNorm bias and then to nonzero keys and values that take softmax mass; block 1 keeps random static prompts. On heads with \(W_oW_v\ne0\) no parameter value is neutral (Thm VI.5(f)): unpointed.

coord_notes.covariance: The channel-shared convolution and the pooling commute with every map on the \(d\) channels and the bottleneck MLP is dense: function-level \(GL\times GL\), as VPT; the spatial grid is the image's own structure. Caveat: the generator's trained per-block LayerNorm (placement not stated) would cut this to the LayerNorm's coordinate symmetries if it acts on the generated prompts; recorded as GLxGL following VPT.
coord_notes.merge: The prompts depend on the input and lengthen the sequence (Thm VI.5(f)).

methods.categorical_reading: VAPT makes each deep prompt an \(X\)-dependent function of the current block's tokens, so in the attention-as-mixture reading the prompt experts become one-hidden-layer functions of the sequence instead of constants. Fibrewise over inputs it is VPT-Deep: every image runs VPT with its own prompts, which is also why no single static prompt reproduces it.

arrows.note: Fibrewise over inputs, into VPT-Deep (prompt outputs discarded per block, as in VAPT), pointed at h_x(q_0) (unpointed slice); block 1's static prompts map to VPT's block-1 prompts.

obstructions.reason: L2P's prompts are piecewise constant in x (hard top-N retrieval from a pool), while VAPT's vary continuously with the block's tokens, so generic VAPT realisations are not L2P's (as for CODA-Prompt).

The rank profile is an output, so the deployed object is a point of the rank filtration rather than a fixed level.

coord_notes.kind: LoRA with a closed-form data-aware start: \(A_0\) the bottom-\(r\) eigenvectors of \(\Omega=\tfrac{\mathrm{tr}(Y_F^{-1})}{N}Z_F^{-1}-\widehat\Delta^\top\widehat\Delta\) and \(B_0=\widehat\Delta A_0^\top\), with \(\widehat\Delta=-DGZ_F^{-1}\), \(D=\mathrm{Diag}(Y_F^{-1})\) (K-FAC factors).

The start alone is covariant only under \(\mathrm{Mon}(d_{out})\times CO(d_{in})\): \(D\) keeps only the diagonal of \(Y_F^{-1}\), and the orthonormal-row eigenproblem turns the congruence \(\Omega\mapsto h^{-\top}\Omega h^{-1}\) into \(CO\).

methods.categorical_reading: LoRA-DA chooses LoRA's starting subspace by minimising an expected distance to the target weight, which splits into a Fisher-preconditioned bias term and an inverse-Fisher variance term. Its two limits are known pointings: the bias-only, raw-gradient limit is LoRA-One's gradient-SVD start, and the variance-only limit takes \(\mathrm{row}A_0\) from the top input-activation directions, an EVA-type frame. Without the residual subtraction it starts off \(\theta_0\), as LoRA-One does.

obstructions.reason: Same image, but rho(q_0) != theta_0: h = id is only a weak morphism, and the start is a rank-r smooth point rather than the apex (as LoRA-One).
LoRA-GA subtracts its initial adapter (vertex W_0 - P_GA); LoRA-DA does not (vertex W_0). The two cones are incomparable, as in Thm II.2(d).

The LoRA-GA obstruction holds: a generic X has rank(X + P_GA) = 2r > r. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: Each selected weight is replaced by its rank-\(K_i\) truncation and trained as a factored low-rank matrix: a dense step from a Tucker-compressed activation gradient, re-projected by one warm-started subspace iteration. No adapter, and \(W_0\) is not kept.
coord_notes.shape: \(\mathcal M_{\le K_i}\), a cone with vertex at the zero matrix, started at \(\mathrm{SVD}_{K_i}(W_0)\), a smooth point: a translated cone with apex \(0\neq\theta_0\).
coord_notes.base_point: The forward pass uses the truncation from step 0, so \(\rho(q_0)-W_0\) is the truncation error (zero only at \(\varepsilon=1\)): a defect, like LoftQ's attained residual.
coord_notes.gauge: Factors \((L,R)\) with \(L\) re-orthonormalised each step: residual \(O(K_i)\), nearest key GL. The released code keeps the dense \(W\) as the parameter and recomputes \(L,R\) from optimizer-carried state.
coord_notes.covariance: \(K_i\) comes from an explained-variance threshold on \(W_0\)'s spectrum and the start is its truncated SVD: \(CO\times CO\) (OxO). The set \(\mathcal M_{\le K}\) itself is \(GL\times GL\)-invariant.

methods.categorical_reading: WASI is a low-rank reparametrisation of the whole box rather than an adapter: the image is the rank-\(K\) variety itself, whose vertex is the zero matrix, so \(\theta_0\) lies outside the image and the start is its nearest point. Training is a projected-gradient (retraction) scheme on \(\mathcal M_K\) with the gradient assembled from compressed activations, which is where the memory saving comes from.

obstructions.reason: PiSSA keeps the residual W_0 - [W_0]_r (vertex W_0 - [W_0]_r); WASI drops it (vertex 0). Translated cones with distinct vertices are not nested.

Im WASI = M_{<=K}; a generic X of rank K has X - W_0 of rank min(m,n) > r (checked), so X is not in W_0 + M_{<=r} = Im LoRA and Im WASI is not inside Im LoRA. WASI's start is also not theta_0 (truncation defect), so no pointed arrow either.

methods.categorical_reading: TeRA tensorises VeRA: the two diagonal scalings become Kronecker products of mode vectors acting on a frozen, shared random Tucker network, so the number of trained scalars stays near \(d_{in}+d_{out}\) while the rank ceiling rises to full. The cone is still toric and the start still an apex; what changes is the frozen frame, which now carries a tensor structure the network does not have.

methods.categorical_reading: Hybrid-LoRA is a fixed \(\oplus\)-word, full fine-tuning on selected boxes plus LoRA on the others. Its content is the selection rule: a first-order sensitivity of the probe's SVD-form LoRA coefficients, measured under random on/off masks of the other modules, with low sensitivity read as 'a low-rank update is not enough here'.

obstructions.reason: Selected modules receive dense updates of rank up to min(m,n) > 16.
Even on a common selected set, Hybrid-LoRA also moves every unselected module through its LoRA, which Spectrum freezes.

coord_notes.kind: Post hoc and training-free: truncate each task vector (and, for LoRA inputs, flatten its spectrum), express all of them in the polar cover basis \((\widetilde U,\widetilde V)\) of the concatenated singular bases, merge entrywise (TIES with top-0.1% trimming), keep the diagonal \(r\times r\) blocks, map back and scale by a validated \(\alpha\).
coord_notes.shape: The coefficient line \(W_0+\alpha\,\widetilde U(\widetilde M\odot\mathcal M)\widetilde V^\top\), \(d=1\).
coord_notes.base_point: \(\alpha=0\) returns \(W_0\).
coord_notes.gauge: None.
coord_notes.covariance: Truncated SVDs and polar factors are \(CO\times CO\)-covariant, spectral flattening is scale-equivariant, and the entrywise rule acts in cover coordinates that move with the frames: OxO, as TSV-M and KnOTS.
coord_notes.merge: One dense delta of rank \(\le rT\) per matrix.

methods.categorical_reading: DC-Merge merges in TSV-M's whitened cover basis with two extra moves: flattening each LoRA task's spectrum, so that directions rather than energies are merged, and a block-diagonal mask that drops cross-task coordinates. The cover basis contains every task's row and column spaces, so the round trip into it is exact; with task arithmetic inside and no mask the method is just the sum of the smoothed task vectors, and its effect lives in the mask and in rules applied in cover coordinates.

arrows.note: Into LoRA_{rT} pointed at (0, V~^T), a T_A point with orthonormal rows when rT < min(m,n) (LoRA inputs); in the full fine-tuning setting rT can reach min(m,n), outside the strata (as Compress-then-Merge -> LoRA).

obstructions.reason: Spectral flattening (LoRA inputs) and the block mask move the merged delta out of span{Delta_i}.

TSV-M puts each task's own Sigma_i in its diagonal block of the whitened basis; DC-Merge puts the merged cover coordinates there, including cross-task contributions inside each block, so the merged deltas differ.

coord_notes.kind: A family over token prefixes: \(\Delta W_t=\tfrac\alpha r\,\lambda(x_{1:t})\,BA\), with \(\lambda=\mathrm{softplus}(w^\top o_t+b)>0\) read from a width-\(r\) Mamba recurrence over \(Px_1,\dots,Px_t\). MaRA, the paragraph selector, acts on the context before generation and is not a weight-space method.
coord_notes.shape: A causal, stateful scalar gate on one LoRA direction: no single weight-space image.
coord_notes.base_point: \(B_0=0\) gives the frozen function at every token (neutral, as LiME); the gate starts near 1 (bias \(\mathrm{softplus}^{-1}(1)\)), so training starts as LoRA.
coord_notes.gauge: \(GL_r\) on \((B,A)\), since the scalar gate commutes with the rank wire; the gate's Mamba block adds only discrete hidden-unit symmetries.
coord_notes.covariance: The gate reads a dense projection of the box input and the LoRA is dense: function-level \(GL\times GL\).
coord_notes.merge: Token-dependent gate (Thm VI.3); a constant \(\lambda\equiv c\) would merge as \(W_0+c\,\tfrac\alpha rBA\).

methods.categorical_reading: MaLoRA pulls LoRA back along a causal gate that depends on the whole prefix: per token the weight is \(W_0+\tfrac\alpha r\lambda_tBA\), a point on one fixed ray of LoRA's cone, and \(\lambda\equiv1\) is LoRA. It replaces aLoRA's position switch by a learned, content-dependent soft gate that is also active on the prompt.
